Splitting rent with a couple or a shared bedroom

Counting only bedrooms can undercount shared-space use. Counting only people can make two people pay twice for one bedroom. A two-part split helps you account for both.

A practical guide from RentSplit Guide · Worked examples included

Try the rent calculator
THE STARTING POINT

Allocate private-space rent once per bedroom and shared-space rent once per person. Split each bedroom's private cost among its occupants.

1. Separate bedroom access from shared access

Choose an agreed fraction of rent for private bedrooms and another for access to the living room, kitchen, and other shared spaces. Divide the shared portion by people. Allocate the private portion by room area or agreed room values, then divide each room's private charge among its occupants.

This is a negotiation tool. People may value privacy, bathroom access, working space, or household congestion differently. Try the method and discuss the resulting payments before settling on it.

2. Calculate a couple-plus-one example

Consider a $2,400 apartment with two equal-sized bedrooms. A couple occupies one and a single roommate occupies the other. They agree that 50% of rent covers shared access and 50% covers bedrooms.

  • Shared access: $1,200 ÷ 3 people = $400 per person.
  • Private space: $1,200 ÷ 2 equal rooms = $600 per room.
  • Each partner pays $400 + $300 = $700.
  • The single roommate pays $400 + $600 = $1,000.

The couple pays $1,400 together, and the three payments total $2,400. If utilities are $180 and shared equally, each person adds $60. Different room areas or a different shared portion produce a different result.

3. Adjust for unequal bedrooms

If the couple's room is larger, use its share of total bedroom area when dividing the private portion. Then divide that room's private charge between the couple. Only count the area once.

Person's rent = shared portion ÷ people + their share of their room's private charge

The homepage calculator divides rent equally by person. Use the steps here when your agreement gives separate values to private rooms and shared access. The room-size guide explains the underlying area calculation.

4. Agree on bills, guests, and changes

Decide which costs follow people and which follow rooms. Internet can be divided per person; a reserved parking space can go to its user. A couple may choose how they divide their combined payment privately, provided the household receives the agreed total.

Discuss what happens if an occupant moves out, a partner becomes a permanent resident, or a room changes hands. Set a date for reviewing the split. Also check occupancy terms in the lease: a payment arrangement does not grant permission to add occupants.

Common questions

Should a couple pay exactly double?

There is no universal rule. Paying twice a single person's share may overvalue access to a single bedroom. A per-room and per-person combination makes the tradeoff explicit.

Should both partners pay utilities?

If utilities are shared per person, each resident contributes. Agree separately on any fixed charges or identifiable individual costs.
